note: For deer, foxes and other long-legged runners; a hare runs with `bound`. Transverse gallop: the hind feet land one after the other, then the front feet one after the other, then a suspension. Each pair is split by a fifth of the cycle so the legs read as alternating, not paired as in a bound. The back flexes once per stride and the body rises once, which is why bobFreq drops to 1 here.
